title: Sky may unilaterally suspend or terminate an Accord on its own determination of misalignment
content:
A.2.8.3.2.3 is the widest of the four carve-outs from mutual consent: Sky Governance may act "where Sky Governance determines that the Accord, or a party's conduct under it, is misaligned with the Sky Ecosystem," with misalignment "includ[ing], but ... not limited to, circumstances where maintaining the Accord would compromise the safety of the Sky Ecosystem or its users."

Three features make it powerful. The judge is Sky Governance itself, not the Core Council or an arbitrator. The standard is alignment, which A.0's framework explicitly concedes cannot be measured deterministically. And the enumeration is open-ended, so the safety example bounds nothing.

This sits in real tension with the mutual consent requirement of A.2.8.3.1. Read together, a counterparty's contractual protection is strong against ordinary renegotiation and weak against an alignment determination — and since alignment is contested by construction, the ceiling on Sky's discretion is political rather than textual.

That is arguably the intended design: the Atlas treats unchecked misalignment as leading to governance attack or financial collapse, so an emergency exit that cannot be blocked by the misaligned party is necessary. But it means counterparties are contracting on Sky's continued judgment of their alignment, and should read the mutual-consent clause as protection against convenience, not against conviction.

The narrower carve-outs are better bounded: administrative corrections (A.2.8.3.2.1) are permitted only where they "do not alter the rights, obligations, or commercial terms of any party" and are limited to typos, formatting, and reference updates; implementation of a Core Council dispute decision (A.2.8.3.2.2) requires a prior adjudication.
description: The exception requires no counterparty consent, no dispute-resolution finding and no enumerated breach — misalignment 'includes, but is not limited to' threats to ecosystem or user safety.
